headline: 15 games, two draws, one rout: the weekend in full
dek: Philadelphia ran riot in San Diego while St. Louis put four past Minnesota; the East split points all over the map.
body: Red Bull New York won the only Eastern game of Saturday, taking three points from Columbus 1-0. D.C. and Atlanta shared a goalless draw, FC Cincinnati and Charlotte traded three apiece, and Inter Miami and Nashville finished 2-2. Orlando thumped Toronto 3-0. Out West on Sunday, Sporting Kansas City beat LAFC 3-1, St. Louis edged Minnesota 4-2, Colorado edged CF Montréal 1-0, San Jose held Houston 1-0, and New England left Chicago with a 2-1 win. Austin FC won at Vancouver 2-1. Real Salt Lake fell to NYCFC 0-2. LA Galaxy and Seattle drew 1-1. On Monday, Philadelphia Union closed the weekend with a 5-0 thrashing at San Diego.

headline: RSL doubles down; three players exit MLS
dek: Real Salt Lake added two players at the window's close while Houston, LAFC, and Minnesota each registered a departure.
body: Real Salt Lake signed Serbian winger Dušan Žagar on a permanent transfer from FK IMT Belgrade and added midfielder Taylor Booth on loan from FC Twente. St. Louis CITY SC brought in U.S. international forward Damion Downs on loan from Southampton. On the departures side, Houston Dynamo transferred midfielder Ondřej Lingr to Polish Ekstraklasa side Korona Kielce after 930 minutes this season. Stephen Eustáquio, who logged 720 minutes for LAFC, has moved on to Swansea City. James Rodríguez has left Minnesota United after 480 minutes; he is a free agent.

headline: Musa holds an 18-goal lead as rivals close
dek: FC Dallas's striker sits three clear at the top; two players are deadlocked for second.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the goals table with 18 on the season, three ahead of Sam Surridge (Nashville SC) and Nicolás Fernández (NYCFC), who are tied at 15. In assists, Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC fronts the field with 10; Evander (FC Cincinnati) and Son Heung-Min (LAFC) sit at nine apiece. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver Whitecaps leads the tackles chart with 100, well clear of Yannick Bright (Inter Miami, 72) and Silvan Hefti (D.C. United, 61).

headline: Fernández and Guilherme are beating the model by 6.6
dek: Atlanta's Almirón is the league's biggest finisher in debt; Son sits nearly five goals below his expected return.
body: Nicolás Fernández (NYCFC) and Guilherme (Houston Dynamo) share the largest positive gap in the league, each outperforming their xG by 6.6 goals, Fernández at 15 goals on 8.4 xG, Guilherme at 13 on 6.4. At the other end, Atlanta's Miguel Almirón has scored four goals against an xG of 8.9, a deficit of 4.9. Son Heung-Min of LAFC has five goals on 9.8 xG, running 4.8 behind the model.

headline: Philadelphia rout Cincy 5-0; Vancouver blank Galaxy 3-0
dek: A brutal week for FC Cincinnati and LA Galaxy as the league's heaviest defeats come from familiar Eastern and Western rivals.
body: Philadelphia Union handed FC Cincinnati a 5-0 defeat at home on Sept. 9, the widest margin of the week. Vancouver Whitecaps answered on Sept. 10 with a 3-0 shutout of LA Galaxy. D.C. United took three points twice, beating Columbus 2-1 and holding Atlanta to a goalless draw. Orlando City went six points from two matches, winning 3-2 at Atlanta before blanking Toronto 3-0. Red Bull New York collected back-to-back road wins at NYCFC and Columbus. San Jose earned a late-week home win over Houston, 1-0, while Sporting Kansas City downed LAFC 3-1.

headline: Six roster moves close the secondary window
dek: Three arrivals and three departures reshape squads as the secondary transfer window shuts.
body: Inter Miami CF added Paraguayan midfielder Matías Galarza on loan from River Plate through the end of the 2026 season. Minnesota United brought in winger Cherrion Valerius on loan from Dutch side NAC Breda. New England Revolution signed American center back Joshua Wynder on loan from SL Benfica. On the departure side, Columbus Crew transferred midfielder Max Arfsten to EFL Championship club Middlesbrough. Colorado Rapids declined the permanent option on winger Alexis Manyoma, who returns to Club Estudiantes de La Plata after logging 810 minutes. NYCFC defender Strahinja Tanasijević, 1,230 minutes this season, has also left the club.

headline: Musa leads at 18; Surridge and Fernández tied at 15
dek: FC Dallas's striker holds a three-goal cushion with the season in its final stretch.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas sits atop the scoring chart with 18 goals. Sam Surridge of Nashville SC and Nicolás Fernández of New York City FC share second place at 15 apiece. In assists, Evander (FC Cincinnati), Joaquín Pereyra (Minnesota United), and Anders Dreyer (San Diego FC) are level at 10. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver Whitecaps dominates the tackles column with 97, well clear of Yannick Bright of Inter Miami at 72 and Silvan Hefti of D.C. United at 61.

headline: Nashville lead East at 54 pts; Vancouver top the West
dek: Both conference leaders have conceded only 21 goals all season, the joint-best record in MLS.
body: Nashville SC head the Eastern Conference with 54 points on a 16W-6D-3L record and 50 goals scored against only 21 conceded. Vancouver Whitecaps lead the West with 46 points (14W-4D-5L), 52 goals for and 21 against. Inter Miami CF carry the league's most prolific attack at 61 goals scored. Nashville's defense, also 21 goals allowed, matches Vancouver's, the two best marks in the division. Simon Becher (St. Louis, 7G vs. 11.0 xG) and Germán Berterame (Inter Miami, 7G vs. 11.0 xG) are the season's biggest xG underperformers, each sitting 4.0 goals below expectation.

headline: Philadelphia routs Cincinnati 5-0 in week's biggest result
dek: Fourteen matches across Sept. 9-10 produced five home losses and one of the season's most lopsided scorelines.
body: Philadelphia Union beat FC Cincinnati 5-0 at home, the widest margin of the midweek round. Orlando City won 3-2 at Atlanta United, Charlotte FC took three points from CF Montreal with a 2-1 away victory, and D.C. United edged Columbus Crew 2-1. Toronto FC beat Nashville SC 2-1. On Sept. 10, Vancouver Whitecaps shut out LA Galaxy 3-0, LAFC blanked Red Bull New York 2-0, and New England Revolution won 2-1 at New York City FC. Houston Dynamo beat Real Salt Lake 2-1. FC Dallas won 2-1 at Minnesota United. San Jose Earthquakes took three road points, winning 3-2 at San Diego FC. Austin and Colorado drew 1-1, Chicago and Inter Miami drew 1-1, and Portland and St. Louis drew 2-2.

headline: Three out, three in as clubs reshape rosters before run-in
dek: Atlanta, Austin, and FC Dallas each lost a player to Europe while Houston, LAFC, and Inter Miami added depth.
body: Defender Stian Gregersen left Atlanta United for Malmö FF of Sweden's Allsvenskan after logging 1,500 minutes this season. Winger Jayden Nelson, 1,080 minutes at Austin FC, was transferred to Bolton Wanderers of the English Championship. Forward Louicius Deedson departed FC Dallas for Ligue 2 side FC Sochaux-Montbéliard after 660 minutes in MLS. On the inbound side, Houston Dynamo signed South African striker Lyle Foster on loan from Burnley FC through June 2027 with a purchase option. LAFC acquired 20-year-old Brazilian forward Thayllon Roberth on loan from Avaí FC through June 2027 with a purchase option.

headline: Musa leads at 18 goals; Evander chases with double figures in two columns
dek: FC Dallas's striker holds a four-goal buffer at the top, while Cincinnati's Evander is the only player in both the goals and assists top three.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the golden boot race with 18 goals. Evander (FC Cincinnati) and Tai Baribo (D.C. United) are tied for second at 14. In assists, Evander and Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC share the lead at 10, with Son Heung-Min of LAFC one back at nine. Evander's presence in both top-three lists makes him the most complete attacker in either conference by the numbers. In tackles, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas is dominant at 97, nearly 30 clear of Inter Miami's Yannick Bright (66) and D.C.'s Silvan Hefti (60).

headline: Guilherme runs 6.6 goals above xG; St. Louis pair both trail their numbers
dek: Houston's Guilherme and NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández are outperforming their models, while two St. Louis forwards are well short of expected output.
body: Houston Dynamo forward Guilherme has scored 13 goals against an xG of 6.4, a plus-6.6 overperformance. NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández is 14 goals against 8.3 xG, plus-5.7. At the other end, St. Louis CITY SC carry two significant underperformers: Simon Becher has 7 goals against an xG of 10.9, minus-3.9, and Rafael Navarro has 12 goals against 15.6 xG, minus-3.6. Nashville SC lead the East at 53 points on a 16-5-3 record; Vancouver Whitecaps top the West with 46 points at 14-4-5. Nashville also hold the league's best defense at 19 goals allowed, while Inter Miami lead all clubs with 59 goals scored.
